title: Rabbi Levi bar Chayta
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Moed Katan 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.29a.2-5), he said: “Someone taking leave of the dead should not say, ‘Go to peace,’ but ‘Go in peace.’ Someone taking leave of the living should say, ‘Go to peace,’ as it is written,” etc. Afterward it says: “And Rabbi Levi said”—“bar Chita,” according to a manuscript cited in Dikdukei Soferim—“Anyone who leaves the synagogue for the study hall merits receiving the Divine Presence, as it is written,” etc.[^1]

In [Yerushalmi Shabbat 6:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.6.9.15), Rabbi Levi bar Chayuta said, concerning the words of Rabbi Berekhya in the name of Rabbi Abba bar Kahana: “Has He not already done so in this world? This is what is written,” etc. In [Yerushalmi Sotah 7:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.7.1.5), Rabbi Levi bar Chita went to Caesarea and heard people reciting the Shema in Greek. He wished to stop them; Rabbi Yosi heard and became angry. The statement is cited under the dictionary entry Aleksnin, where the name is Rabbi Levi bar Chorta.[^2]
In [Bereishit Rabbah 55:7 (Hyman cites 55:5)](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.55.7), Rabbi Levi bar Chayta said: “Twice it is written, ‘Go forth,’” etc.[^3]

In [Bereishit Rabbah 39:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.39.11), Rabbi Levi bar Chavyat and Rabbi Abba, the son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, said, etc. Perhaps the name should read bar Chavit or Chayta.[^4]

notes.text: The linked Moed Katan names Levi bar Chayta in the farewell ruling and gives “Rabbi Levi” in the next saying. Hyman supplies bar Chita for the latter from Dikdukei Soferim. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2348&lang=en) also refers to the end of Moed Katan.

The linked Yerushalmi gives Chayuta in Shabbat and Chita in Sotah. In the latter, Levi hears the Shema read in Greek and Rabbi Yosi hears of his objection. Hyman reports Chorta in the Arukh. Guggenheimer’s note records a different Arukh form, bar Hazota.
The linked midrash gives the two uses of lekh lekha, “Go forth,” at Genesis 12:1 and 22:2.
The linked Bereshit Rabbah has חוית, vocalized Chivyat, beside Hyman’s חויית. Hyman proposes חוית or Chayta. The Heilprin entry linked above treats the comparable Chavit form as a scribal error.
